idea: The one habit that fixed my mornings
text:
I used to start my mornings reacting to everything around me.

I pick one task to prep the night before. I choose something small like setting out my clothes or writing a single priority. It cuts decision fatigue before I even open my eyes. That shift keeps my brain from racing. I look at my desk or closet and pick one item. If I skip it, I notice a slower start and reset the next night.

I get light before I touch a screen. I step toward a window or step outside for a minute. That natural light sets my rhythm better than scrolling does. It keeps my focus steady through the first hour. I watch for brightness hitting my face. If I grab my phone first, I swap it for a look outside.

That one move changed how my day unfolds.
title: The one habit that fixed my mornings
